SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.62
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a prototypical aromatic Raman pattern: a very strong ring-breathing band at 1004 cm⁻¹ and a strong ring C=C stretch near 1618 cm⁻¹, plus aromatic C–H stretches around 3081 cm⁻¹ (consistent with GFQ-003). The out-of-plane C–H deformation at 763 cm⁻¹ accompanied by a lower band near 665 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a monosubstituted benzene ring, which fits candidate 10. In contrast, candidates bearing carbonyl or amide functions (1–6, 8, 9) should show a distinct C=O/amide I band near ~1650–1720 cm⁻¹ and/or N–H stretches near 3300–3400 cm⁻¹, which are not observed. Halogenated candidates (2–6, 9) would also typically display stronger characteristic C–X stretches; the low-frequency features here are better assigned to ring modes rather than heavy-atom stretches. Thus, the monosubstituted aromatic with no carbonyl/N–H/O–H (candidate 10) best matches the observed Raman features.
